skill.name: role-creator
skill.description: Create and update Codex custom agent TOML files with explicit scope, model, reasoning, and validation steps.
skill.summary: Build focused Codex custom agents as standalone TOML role files.
skill.author: am-will

security_audit.summary: The skill is a legitimate Codex custom-agent authoring tool, but it intentionally writes persistent Codex configuration under hidden agent paths. Most Markdown command and documentation URL detections are false positives, while hidden config writes, developer-instructions file reads, and MCP filter construction require clear warnings and tighter validation.

remediation.issue: Persistent writes to hidden Codex configuration paths
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before writing under ~/.codex or project .codex directories, and show the exact target path before changes.

remediation.issue: User-controlled MCP names are interpolated into a generated tomlq filter
remediation.suggestion: Validate MCP server names with a safe identifier regex and bind names through jq or tomlq variables instead of string concatenation.

remediation.issue: Developer instructions can be loaded from any user-provided file path
remediation.suggestion: Document that file contents are copied into the agent config and require confirmation for hidden, home, or system paths.

remediation.issue: Optional runtime settings can expand agent filesystem and network authority
remediation.suggestion: Keep minimal defaults and warn before enabling danger-full-access, network access, live web search, or MCP server changes.

semantic_findings.title: Filter Injection in MCP Server Names
semantic_findings.description: scripts/write_role_config.sh trims names from --mcp-enable and --mcp-disable, then interpolates them into the tomlq filter. A crafted name containing filter syntax could alter fields outside the intended mcp_servers entry.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The CSV values are user-controlled and only trimmed before being inserted into the filter string. No name validation or jq variable binding protects the generated expression.

semantic_findings.title: Permissive Runtime Options in Persistent Roles
semantic_findings.description: The skill can write sandbox_mode, network_access, web_search, and MCP settings into persistent Codex role files. This is legitimate functionality, but unsafe choices can expand a custom agent filesystem or network authority.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both the command interface and the skill contract list optional runtime permission controls. The skill defaults to minimal settings, so the issue is permission disclosure and confirmation rather than malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Custom agent setup can be error-prone when paths and TOML fields differ. This skill creates, updates, and validates Codex role files with clear inputs.
actual_capabilities: Collects required role name, description, model, reasoning effort, instructions, and scope before writing.
Creates standalone TOML files for global or project-scoped Codex custom agents.
Supports optional nickname candidates, sandbox mode, web search, network access, and MCP toggles.
Updates a Codex role declaration and can back up the existing config before replacing it.
Validates role declarations and role TOML files with jq and tomlq checks.
limitations: Requires explicit user inputs before it can safely write a role file.
Shell helpers depend on jq and tomlq being installed in the environment.
Can write to hidden Codex configuration locations when global or project paths are selected.
Does not verify external MCP packages, API permissions, or runtime model availability.

use_cases.title: Create a focused reviewer role
use_cases.description: Define a project-scoped reviewer agent with clear instructions, model settings, and validation before use.

use_cases.title: Standardize team agent templates
use_cases.description: Prepare repeatable role files for common tasks such as review, research, documentation, and planning.

use_cases.title: Control agent runtime permissions
use_cases.description: Build roles with explicit sandbox, web search, and MCP settings when a workflow needs controlled capabilities.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Role
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a simple custom agent.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a project-scoped Codex agent named reviewer. Use medium reasoning, a concise description, and narrow developer instructions for code review.

prompt_templates.title: Add Display Names
prompt_templates.scenario: Add optional nickname candidates for a role.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a global Codex agent named researcher with three nickname candidates. Confirm the output path before writing the TOML file.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Existing Files
prompt_templates.scenario: Check a role declaration and role TOML file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate my existing Codex role named planner. Check the declaration, required fields, unsupported keys, and TOML parse status.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Advanced Runtime Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a project agent for release analysis with read-only sandboxing, cached web search, and no MCP servers unless I approve each one.

output_examples.input: Create a project reviewer role with high reasoning and concise review instructions.
output_examples.output: The skill confirms the role name, scope, model, reasoning level, and target path. It writes the role file and reports validation status.

output_examples.input: Validate a role that fails to start when called by agent type.
output_examples.output: The skill checks the active scope, confirms the role file path, validates required fields, and explains the missing or unsupported setting.

output_examples.input: Create a research role with optional web search enabled.
output_examples.output: The skill asks for explicit approval of the web search setting, writes the requested role, and notes the enabled runtime capability.

best_practices: Confirm role scope and target path before writing any global or project configuration file.
Keep developer instructions narrow, operational, and tied to the role purpose.
Use minimal optional settings unless the workflow requires sandbox, search, or MCP changes.
anti_patterns: Creating global agents without clear user approval of the hidden Codex path.
Enabling broad sandbox, network, search, or MCP settings by default.
Putting secret values directly inside role configuration files or developer instructions.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates standalone TOML files for Codex custom agents and can validate related role declarations.

faq.question: Does it support Claude and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatibility, but the role files target Codex custom agents.

faq.question: Can it create project-scoped agents?
faq.answer: Yes. It can write role files under a project .codex directory when that scope is selected.

faq.question: Can it create global agents?
faq.answer: Yes. Global agents use hidden Codex paths under the user home directory and should be confirmed before writing.

faq.question: Can it enable network or web search settings?
faq.answer: Yes, when requested. The safer default is to omit those settings unless the user explicitly approves them.

faq.question: What tools are required for validation?
faq.answer: The shell validation helpers expect jq and tomlq to be available in the environment.
